structure_reference: partner_dv_dbt / travel_dv_dbt -- models/staging/<lob>/ and models/automate_dv/{standard/{stitched,staging,hubs,links,satellites,references},augmented/{staging,satellites}}. Followed exactly; no resolver, hop-view, unpivot, hub-feed or reject_log layer.

inputs_pinned.note: EXACTLY the mapping maximus_health_v3_dv_dbt was built from. The bundle has moved since: its live 04_column_map.json is a later revision (r1 fixes). v3's bytes survive in the bundle as 04_column_map.pre_r1fix1.json, md5 identical to the md5 v3 recorded; same for KEY_FUNCTIONS and BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS. Every file is read by md5, never by name.

not_read.SourceMapping_Skill/Maximum Health Mappi: the mapper's later revision (md5 f3f1fd8284b4aac8f10ef216e3dcf87d). Not v3's mapping, so not this build's.

central_view_rule.verbatim: 1. we create a central view from source tables (by joining them , max upto 10). The join are selected so that it can feed sat as a whole (one or moew). That is we do not split sat across these views. Restriction of 10 can be broken if a sat needs more than source tables to build. If a view as less source tables join, we add more tables to it efficiently so that new sats can be built.
central_view_rule.hub_and_link_extension_verbatim: the views will have hub keys -- effectively each sat is primary key goes to hub -- so hub has to come from there, 2nd the links will also be from same view , as different hub keys and sat populatin comes from there
central_view_rule.what_counts_toward_the_limit: the source tables whose rows FEED the view (each contributes branches). Ancestor and sibling tables joined only to resolve a spine walk are lookups for a key, not sources of the view's rows; they are listed per view as walk tables and are not counted.

spine.climb: child.PARENT_KEY_HASH = parent.KEY_HASH, one join per REAL level (the named hops are waypoints; skipped levels are expanded from the graph). Direction is read from the graph, never from the arrow.
spine.foreign_key_start: spine[FOREIGN_KEY -> X] is joined as child.FOREIGN_KEY = parent.KEY_HASH at the first real level, then climbed. The bundle does not define FOREIGN_KEY; this reading is registered for the mapper to confirm.
spine.descend: A >> T.COL: T must be a descendant of the climb's end. Resolved through a subquery grouped by the ancestor's KEY_HASH, and the value is taken ONLY when exactly one distinct value exists -- a 1:N descend yields NULL (the row is rejected), never a pick.

normalise_note: normalise() is on the map's RATIFIED function allowlist (KEY_FUNCTIONS s6) and is defined nowhere in the bundle or this workspace. 'emit' carries the ratified expressions verbatim and declares a precondition: a Snowflake function normalise(varchar) must exist before dbt run. 'refuse' would drop every key that calls it.

directives.surrogate_child_keys: child_key_components[].leg_backing == 'surrogate' -> the row is QUARANTINED (refused, registered); never loaded as a multi-active history (BUILD_INSTRUCTIONS s2, KEY_FUNCTIONS s7.11).
directives.do_not_build: honoured at BOTH block scope and component scope.
directives.reference_decode: build_directive == true on a reference_decode row -> refused; no decode is available, and a raw code in a label attribute is wrong data.
directives.hard_stop_precondition: resolved_key.precondition_severity == 'hard_stop' -> refused until the stated data check is run.
directives.degenerate: a key is NULLed when it equals its own resolved_key.degenerate_value or is empty; a constant_on_blank_row pure literal is accepted (KEYING s9, KEY_FUNCTIONS s2.3).
directives.spine_display: the 'spine:' display form in child-key values is never executed; a template operand in that form resolves only when the row's own resolved_key carries a walk to the same destination column.
directives.operand_separators: '#' and '@' inside one leg value are operand separators, re-joined with the separator preserved; legs are split only on ' | ' at brace depth zero.

conventions.role_satellites: satellites on the one-hub LNK_PARTY_ROLE are built off HUB_PARTY with a literal ROLE_TYPE_CK (ratified role-special pattern)
conventions.load_datetime: !CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()  -- as the reference projects write it, by the user's instruction
conventions.payload_names: UPPER_SNAKE of the data_7.js attribute name
conventions.hub_business_key_column: <HUB>_BK (same as health_consolidated_v5_dv_dbt; one view-level stage carries several hubs)

staging_casts: every column nullif(trim(to_varchar("COL")), '') aliased lower-case, as health_consolidated_v5_dv_dbt does. KEY_HASH / PARENT_KEY_HASH / FOREIGN_KEY are join keys and are carried the same way.
refusals_not_fallbacks: A key, child key, walk or attribute that cannot be resolved from the pinned inputs is REFUSED and registered with whose call it is.
